reviews.title: A solid 5 star CPU cooler
reviews.comment: I put this on an 5900XT (16 cores, 32 threads). It runs cool, it's quiet, well made, and it looks nice. Temps have never gotten close to throttling levels so far. It's far more reasonably priced than water coolers. Mounting wasn't difficult, but you need to change the motherboard fan mounts. Examine the instructions carefully as the mounting brackets are not interchangable, and need to be in a specific orientation. Be aware the heat pipes extend out over the RAM, and there may be clearance issues with some RAM modules. It's also pretty large, and it may not fit in smaller cases.
reviews.author: James D.

reviews.title: Excellent cooling performance and very quiet operation
reviews.comment: The be quiet! Pure Rock Pro 3 Black CPU air cooler exceeded my expectations with its strong cooling performance, solid build quality, and impressively quiet operation, making it a great upgrade for anyone who wants reliable airflow and lower temperatures without adding a lot of noise to their system.

reviews.title: Super quiet.
reviews.comment: Havent had a single issue with this fan. I cant even hear a difference when the computer is on or off. Super easy to install. Its a little large and makes viewing the RGB RAM i bought a little difficult but it does the job it was purchased to do.

reviews.title: quite and efficient
reviews.comment: Used this on a Ryzen 9 7900X. I wasn't sure if I should go with an air cooler or AIO, but I went ahead with the Pure Rock Pro 3, and it delivered outstanding thermals. HWMonitor recorded: CPU Package: ~65°C under a 3-hour heavy load Core Temps: 40–50°C range across all cores SoC: ~53°C Boost Clocks: up to 5.4–5.5 GHz with no throttling For a 170W processor, these results, in my opinion, are excellent. It's quiet, efficient, and surprisingly powerful for an air cooler. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Ashok Upadhaya
